$comment: Governing document, first half: Organization, Governance, Economics. Maps to the Operating Agreement for an LLC and the Bylaws for a C-Corp — the `entities` tag decides which clauses appear.

clauses.title: Formation and Term
clauses.rationale: Establishes the parties and the effective date, and ties the governing document back to the charter filing.
clauses.body: This {{govDoc}} is entered into as of {{date}} (the “Effective Date”) by and among the Company and {{founderList}} (each a “{{ownerSing}}” and collectively the “{{ownerTerm}}”). The Company was formed by filing a {{charterDoc}} with the Secretary of State of {{formStateLong}}.

clauses.title: Principal Office
clauses.rationale: The principal place of business is distinct from the registered office and may be in a different state.
clauses.body: The Company’s principal place of business shall be in {{opStateLong}}, or at such other location as the {{ownerTerm}} may designate. The registered office is the address stated in <<xr:charter_agent>> and need not be the principal place of business.

clauses.title: Capital Contributions
clauses.rationale: Fixes what each Member actually put in, which is the basis for percentage interests and for capital accounts.
clauses.body: Each {{ownerSing}} shall make the initial [[capital contribution]] set forth on Schedule A. No {{ownerSing}} shall be required to make any additional contribution except as approved under <<xr:gov_voting>>. A {{ownerSing}} who fails to make a required contribution shall not thereby become liable to any other {{ownerSing}}, but the Company may pursue any remedy available at law.

clauses.title: Issuance of Stock
clauses.rationale: Stock is issued by board resolution against consideration actually received. Issuing before payment creates a defect that surfaces in diligence.
clauses.body: The Board may issue shares of Common Stock up to the number authorized in <<xr:charter_shares>>, in each case for consideration determined by the Board and actually received by the Company. Certificates are not required; uncertificated shares shall be recorded in the Company’s stock ledger.

clauses.title: Ownership Interests
clauses.rationale: States the ownership split and points to the schedule that carries the actual numbers, so the split can change without amending the whole document.
clauses.body: As of the Effective Date, ownership is divided among the {{ownerTerm}} in the percentages set forth on Schedule A, totaling one hundred percent (100%). {{ownerSplitNote}} Schedule A shall be updated to reflect any issuance or transfer permitted under this {{govDoc}}.

clauses.title: Tax Classification
clauses.benchmark: Present in 58% of multi-member LLC agreements
clauses.rationale: Tax classification is left to the default unless stated. Saying it out loud prevents one owner from filing an election the others did not agree to.
clauses.body: The {{ownerTerm}} intend the Company to be treated as {{taxDefault}} for federal income tax purposes and shall not file an election inconsistent with that treatment without unanimous approval under <<xr:gov_voting>>.

clauses.title: Management and Voting
clauses.rationale: Separating ordinary decisions from protected ones is the single most useful thing an operating agreement does.
clauses.body: Ordinary business decisions require the approval of {{ownerTerm}} holding a majority of ownership percentages. The following require unanimous approval: amending this {{govDoc}}, admitting a new {{ownerSing}}, selling substantially all assets, incurring indebtedness outside the ordinary course, and dissolving the Company.

clauses.title: Board of Directors
clauses.rationale: The board manages the corporation; stockholders elect it and approve a short list of fundamental changes. Conflating the two is the most common error in founder-drafted bylaws.
clauses.body: The business of the Company shall be managed by or under the direction of the Board. Directors are elected by the {{ownerTerm}} and serve until a successor is elected or until earlier resignation or removal. The following require {{ownerTerm}} approval in addition to Board approval: amending the {{charterDoc}}, merging or selling substantially all assets, and dissolving the Company.

clauses.title: Officers
clauses.rationale: Officers hold delegated authority. Without a stated scope, counterparties cannot tell who may bind the company.
clauses.body: The Board shall appoint a {{principalTitle}} and a Secretary, and may appoint such other officers as it determines. Each officer serves at the pleasure of the Board and has the authority the Board delegates in writing. No officer may bind the Company to an obligation outside the ordinary course without Board approval.

clauses.title: Managers
clauses.rationale: Above two owners, day-to-day decision-making by full member vote becomes impractical. Manager-managed structure matches how the company actually operates.
clauses.body: The {{ownerTerm}} shall appoint one or more Managers to conduct the Company’s day-to-day business. A Manager need not be a {{ownerSing}}. Managers act by majority where more than one serves, and may be removed with or without cause by the vote required for ordinary decisions under <<xr:gov_voting>>.

clauses.title: Meetings and Quorum
clauses.rationale: Without a stated quorum the statutory default applies, and the statutory default is frequently not what small teams expect.
clauses.body: A [[quorum]] consists of {{ownerTerm}} holding a majority of ownership percentages. Meetings may be held by any means through which all participants can hear one another, and participation by such means constitutes presence in person.

clauses.title: Action by Written Consent
clauses.rationale: Small companies almost never hold real meetings. Written consent is how decisions actually get made, and it needs express authorization.
clauses.body: Any action that may be taken at a meeting may instead be taken by written consent signed by those whose approval would be required at a meeting. Consents may be signed in counterparts and delivered electronically, and are effective when the last required signature is delivered.

clauses.title: Sole Owner Provisions
clauses.rationale: Single-owner entities are the most common target for veil-piercing. The formalities matter more here, not less.
clauses.body: The Company has a single {{ownerSing}}. All actions requiring approval may be taken by the sole {{ownerSing}} acting alone and evidenced in writing. The {{ownerSing}} shall observe entity formalities and maintain separate books and accounts; commingling personal and Company funds may support an argument for [[piercing the veil|piercing the veil]].

clauses.title: Standard of Care
clauses.rationale: States the duty owed. Delaware permits an LLC to modify or eliminate fiduciary duties; doing so silently is worse than doing so expressly.
clauses.body: Each {{ownerSing}}, Manager, and officer shall discharge their duties in good faith, with the care an ordinarily prudent person in a like position would exercise, and in a manner reasonably believed to be in the best interests of the Company. This standard may be modified only by an express written amendment adopted under <<xr:gov_amend>>.

clauses.title: Conflicts of Interest
clauses.benchmark: Present in 62% of multi-owner governing documents
clauses.rationale: Related-party transactions are normal in small companies. A disclosure-and-approval path is what keeps them from becoming a claim later.
clauses.body: A {{ownerSing}}, Manager, or officer may transact business with the Company provided the material facts of the relationship are disclosed in advance and the transaction is approved by the disinterested {{ownerTerm}}. An approved transaction shall not be voidable solely because of the relationship.

clauses.title: Books and Records
clauses.rationale: Inspection rights exist by statute in every state in this library. Stating the mechanics avoids a dispute about process on top of the underlying dispute.
clauses.body: The Company shall maintain complete books and records at its principal office. Each {{ownerSing}} may inspect them upon five (5) business days’ written notice for any purpose reasonably related to their interest, at their own expense and during normal business hours.

clauses.title: Amendment
clauses.rationale: An amendment provision that points back to the voting clause keeps the approval thresholds in one place.
clauses.body: This {{govDoc}} may be amended only by a writing signed by the {{ownerTerm}} required to approve amendments under <<xr:@approval>>. No course of dealing or oral statement amends this {{govDoc}}.

clauses.title: Board Committees
clauses.benchmark: Present in 34% of pre-Series A bylaws
clauses.rationale: Rarely needed before a priced round, but adding the authority now costs nothing and saves a bylaw amendment when an investor asks for an audit or compensation committee.
clauses.body: The Board may designate one or more committees, each consisting of one or more directors, and may delegate to any committee the authority of the Board except where prohibited by law. Each committee shall keep minutes and report to the Board.

clauses.title: Distributions
clauses.rationale: Distributions are discretionary unless stated otherwise, and the solvency limitation is a statutory constraint worth restating.
clauses.body: Distributions shall be made [[pro rata]] in proportion to ownership percentages, at such times as approved under <<xr:gov_voting>>, provided the Company retains reserves sufficient to meet its obligations as they come due. No distribution shall be made that would render the Company unable to pay its debts as they become due.

clauses.title: Tax Distributions
clauses.benchmark: Present in 73% of multi-member LLC agreements
clauses.rationale: Pass-through income is taxed to the owners whether or not cash is distributed. Without a tax distribution, an owner can owe tax on income they never received.
clauses.body: The Company shall distribute to each {{ownerSing}}, before any other distribution, an amount sufficient to pay the estimated federal and state income tax on that {{ownerSing}}’s allocable share of Company income, calculated at the highest marginal rate applicable to an individual resident in {{opStateLong}}. Tax distributions are advances against future distributions under <<xr:gov_distrib>>.

clauses.title: Allocations of Profit and Loss
clauses.rationale: Allocations and distributions are different things. Silence on allocations invites a mismatch between the K-1 and the cash.
clauses.body: Profits and losses shall be allocated among the {{ownerTerm}} in proportion to their ownership percentages. Allocations are intended to comply with the substantial economic effect requirements of the Treasury Regulations, and the Company’s tax preparer may adjust them as required for that purpose.

clauses.title: Dividends
clauses.rationale: Included for completeness. An early-stage C-Corp will not pay dividends, but the authority should be stated rather than assumed.
clauses.body: The Board may declare dividends out of funds legally available, subject to the rights of any series of [[Preferred Stock|preferred stock]] designated under <<xr:charter_shares>>.

clauses.title: Expense Reimbursement
clauses.benchmark: Present in 47% of comparable governing documents
clauses.rationale: Founders routinely pay company costs personally before there is a bank account. A reimbursement provision makes those advances recoverable and documented.
clauses.body: The Company shall reimburse each {{ownerSing}} for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred on the Company’s behalf, upon submission of documentation and subject to any policy adopted under <<xr:@approval>>. Expenses incurred before the Effective Date are reimbursable if approved and documented within ninety (90) days.
